title: How do four rulers read in hundredths?
description: Four rulers end a few small parts after a whole mark. Each length is written with units and hundredths and then read in words. Keeko doubts the reading and calls the small parts tenths.
teaching_notes: One idea: whole units come first and the extra small parts are hundredths. Watch for students who read thirty seven small parts as thirty seven tenths, and who write three small parts as thirty hundredths.

source: Four rulers show lengths in hundredths: one reaches 37 parts after the 5 mark, another 3 parts after the 15 mark, another 52 parts after the 7 mark and the last 80 parts after the 9 mark. Write each measurement and read it in words.
video_script.why: The child can write a length as units and hundredths and now reads four rulers and says each one in words.
video_script.substitution: The whole mark gives the units and the small parts after it give the hundredths.
video_script.anchor: Four rulers, each ending some small parts after a whole mark, with each unit cut into one hundred parts
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads 37 small parts as 37 tenths, but a unit has only 10 tenths, so 37 small parts are 37 hundredths.
video_script.payoff_line: Each ruler reads whole units and then the extra parts as hundredths

final_answer.spoken: five and thirty seven hundredths, fifteen and three hundredths, seven and fifty two hundredths, and nine and eighty hundredths

maths_rules: 37 parts after the 5 mark is 5 and 37 hundredths, 5 37/100.
3 parts after the 15 mark is 15 and 3 hundredths, 15 3/100; the 3 sits in the hundredths place, not as 30.
80 parts after the 9 mark is 9 80/100, read nine and eighty hundredths.
Slip: 37 small parts are not 37 tenths, because a unit has only 10 tenths.
video_script.design: One idea: whole units first, then the extra small parts as hundredths. Assumes the child can write a length as units and hundredths. Wrong idea: read the small parts as tenths. The four rulers stay all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko reads the first ruler as five and thirty seven tenths, because the small parts look like tenths.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a unit has only ten tenths, so thirty seven tenths cannot fit. These are hundredths, because the unit has one hundred small parts.
